title: Volleyball: Teamwork in the Air
summary: How rotation, timing, communication, and the physics of a good serve or spike make volleyball a team sport built on science.
poll: Good teamwork matters more than individual skill in sports.

versions.title: Hit It Over the Net!
versions.text:
Bump! Set! Spike! The ball flies over the net. Is this just a game? It is science, too!

A man made this game long ago. He lived in the United States. The year was 1895. He first called it mintonette!

Two teams play. Each team has six players. Three stand in front. Three stand in back.

The ball must go over the net. It must not fall on your side. Your team may hit it three times.

A serve starts the play. The server hits the ball hard over the net. The ball can spin as it flies.

When your team wins the serve back, players rotate. They move one spot. This way, everyone gets a turn.

A spike is a strong hit down into the other side. Players jump high to spike the ball hard.

Teammates talk to each other. They call "Mine!" so they do not bump into each other.

Fans in Saudi Arabia love to watch volleyball games by the sea.

MID.prompt: Explain how two different science ideas from the article help a team score a point. Use the words timing and momentum.

MID.modelAnswer: Good timing helps a team score because the hitter must jump at the exact moment the ball is set near the net, meeting it at the peak of the jump. HIGH.prompt: A friend says volleyball is just about jumping high. Write a response using at least three physics ideas from the article to show how science shapes the sport.
checklist: I responded clearly to my friend's claim.
I explained at least three physics ideas from the article.
I used key words such as trajectory, velocity, or coordination correctly.
HIGH.modelAnswer: Volleyball is about far more than jumping high. The angle and spin of a serve shape its trajectory, so a topspin serve dips sharply while a floater wobbles unpredictably, making both hard to read. A spike also depends on velocity, since a hitter who swings quickly at the right moment sends the ball downward at remarkably high speed. Finally, the sport depends on coordination and friction, because teammates must communicate to avoid collisions, and diving players rely on friction between their knee pads and the floor to save a low ball safely.
